data.title: Autodesk initiated with Neutral rating due to near-term AI concerns: Cantor
data.description:
Cantor initiated coverage on Autodesk (ADSK) with a Neutral rating, as the financial services firm believes the rise of artificial intelligence poses a credible threat to the design software stalwart.

"ADSK is the global leader in Design software, with strong franchises in AutoCAD, Revit, Fusion, Civil 3D, Inventor, and Forma," said Cantor analyst Mason Marion in an in-depth investor report. "While AI poses perhaps the most credible threat to these franchises in ADSK's history, we expect the company to endure and grow in the AI era."

"ADSK is not standing by idly, investing in proprietary 3D generative AI models (neural CAD) and infusing Autodesk AI throughout its platform," he added. "Outside of Design, ADSK is leveraging its strong Design franchises to expand into Construction with Forma for Construction ($600m+ TTM rev growing 20%+)."

In addition, Autodesk's recent $3.6B acquisition of MaintainX is expected to increase its total addressable market.

Cantor set a price target of $215 on Autodesk, as it believes the market has already established a fair value for the stock.

data.title: FuelCell Energy started with Neutral rating at Citi as product backlog remains modest
data.description:
FuelCell Energy (FCEL) falls 0.9% in Tuesday's trading as Citi initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and $19 price target, noting progress towards strategic and financial objectives is picking up pace, with demand from hyperscaler data centers and colocation/neocloud providers driving the order pipeline to ~10 GW, and average proposal sizes rising ~3x over the last six months.

The company offers several differentiated strengths, according to Citi's Vikram Bagri, including native DC baseload power, rapid deployment timelines, and more than 20 years of utility-scaleoperating experience, while its molten carbonate platform benefits from a largely U.S.-based supply chain, improved seven-year stack life, better power density, low emissions, chilled-water production, and carbon-capture capabilities.

To leverage the technology and position FuelCell (FCEL) for long-term success, Bagri said management has implemented recent restructurings that should allow operating expenses to grow roughly in line with inflation while the company benefits from strong operating leverage as it grows production and achieves positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2027.

However, FuelCell's (FCEL) product backlog remains modest at ~$109M, and the broader pipeline has yet to convert meaningfully into firm orders, and its ~50% efficiency trails Bloom Energy's SOFC platform, while expanding gas turbine, fuel cell, and engine manufacturing capacity could increase competitive pressure, the analyst said.

data.title: Boeing is said to near deal with Turkish Airlines for 150 737 Max jets
data.description:
Boeing (BA) is nearing an agreement to sell 150 737 Max jets to Turkish Airlines after a dispute over engine maintenance delayed the order, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the negotiations.

The purchase is part of a broader agreement for 225 Boeing (BA) aircraft announced after Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan met U.S. President Donald Trump last year. The Max portion could be finalized as soon as next week.

Turkish Airlines had threatened to switch the order to Airbus amid disagreements with engine manufacturer CFM International over maintenance costs, spare-parts prices and long-term repair risks. CFM is jointly owned by GE Aerospace (GE) and Safran (SAFRF)(SAFRY).

The carrier also sought a leading role in CFM’s maintenance network, which would give it faster access to repair technology for engines used on the 737 Max. It remains unclear whether that request will be included in the final agreement.

A completed order would preserve one of the major Boeing agreements announced by the White House last year. Turkish media have reported that Trump and Erdogan may meet during United Nations gatherings in New York next week.

Turkish Airlines operates more than 400 Boeing and Airbus aircraft. It is also considering regional jets from Embraer and Airbus as well as the larger Boeing 777X and Airbus A350-1000 as it expands its Istanbul hub.

data.title: Hedgeye reiterates RadNet long idea
data.description:
Hedgeye is reiterating its long call on RadNet (RDNT) with the potential for 30% upside.

"The valuation looks stretched against consensus, but we can model upside well into 2027 on several simultaneous secular tailwinds that justify the premium: (1) continued inpatient-to-outpatient imaging migration, (2) mix shift toward high-margin advanced imaging (PET/CT, MRI, and CT), where both volumes and pricing are accelerating on demand from Alzheimer's, Oncology, and Cardiology, and (3) AI tailwinds driving incremental revenue and operating leverage," Hedgeye analyst Tom Tobin wrote in a note.

"Our model puts 2027 total Adj. EBITDA at $500M versus the Street at $421M, roughly 19% ahead. Even into the Q3 2026 print we sit above consensus, at $104M versus the Street's $95M," Tobin added.

Shares of RadNet (RDNT) rose 3.8% on Tuesday and have gained 5.8% this year. 

RadNet (RDNT) is set to present at the Morgan Stanley 24th Annual Global Healthcare conferece in New York on Wednesday.

data.title: West Fraser raised at Raymond James as 'housing recovery not necessary to buy the trees'
data.description:
West Fraser Timber (WFG) gains 2.1% in Tuesday's trading as Raymond James upgraded the wood products company to Outperform from Market Perform with an $85 price target, which also raised Interfor (IFSPF) and Canfor (CFPZF) to Strong Buy, saying a U.S. housing recovery is "not necessary to buy the trees."

After four years of depressed U.S. housing, repair, and renovation activity, Raymond James analyst Daryl Swetlishoff said the supply side "has finally done the heavy lifting to improve balance in North American lumber markets," Canadian shipments have fallen to record lows, capacity has permanently exited the system, and European lumber imports have fallen sharply.

Despite cyclical and seasonal demand headwinds, 2026 results approached "what we consider mid-cycle profitability with our refreshed 3Q26 estimates not too far behind," the analyst wrote.

With lumber equities still trading at or below tangible book value, Swetlishoff said a U.S. housing recovery is not currently priced in the stocks, but the analyst "could see ~30% higher benchmark lumber pricing, translating to 100%-300% theoretical equity upside... hence, we see a compelling asymmetric setup with meaningful upside available before underwriting any macro improvement."

"We recommend investors build full positions now as we head into the 2026-27 seasonal trade," the analyst said.

data.title: Soft August dining traffic weighs on restaurant sector
data.description:
Restaurant stocks are on the defensive Tuesday as industry data showed a meaningful decline in dining traffic, albeit largely driven by the timing of this year’s Labor Day weekend.

According to the  August 2026 Retail and Dining Index from Placer.ai, dining visits were down 2.4% in August, reversing a gradual improvement in June and July after a 2.5% decline in May 2026.

Because of the timing of the Labor Day weekend this year, dining activity that would typically begin in late August was pushed into September with the Labor Day holiday falling on September 7 vs. September 1 in 2025.

The survey also attributes the soft dining trends to macroeconomic conditions, as a gallon of gas exceeded $4 per gallon in August, putting 2026 on track as one of the most expensive years for gas.

Dining traffic was down in every state except California, which saw a slight uptick from a year ago. Notable weakness was seen in Montana, Wyoming, South Dakota, New Mexico, Vermont, and West Virginia.

The pressure on the restaurant sector is weighing on the Consumer Discretionary SPDR ETF (XLY) and Vanguard Consumer Discretionary ETF (VCR).

data.title: Bitcoin, crypto stocks slip as hopes for Clarity Act progress fade
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) fell as much as 4.9% on Tuesday from Monday's high of nearly $80K after a Democratic counteroffer over the Clarity Act dimmed hopes of the digital asset legislation progressing.

The price of the largest cryptocurrency by market cap slid to $76.6K Tuesday afternoon, down 3.0% over the past 24 hours. The low of the day was $75.7K, compared with Monday's high-level mark of $79.6K.

Ethereum (ETH-USD), the second-largest digital token by market cap, dropped 3.9% to $2.44K.

The odds of the Clarity Act becoming law before Jan. 1, 2027, slid to 13% from as high as 39% at 7:27 AM ET. Legislators have been squabbling over the stablecoin legislation for about a year.

A procedural vote to advance the bill to the Senate floor for a full vote is due to take place Tuesday afternoon. Major sticking points included ethics over legislators and the president profiting from stablecoins and other digital assets and whether platforms should be allowed to pay interest on stablecoin holdings.

Cryptocurrencies and crypto stocks climbed on Monday after Republicans' final draft of the legislation included some ethics restrictions on conflicts of interest. It would also give the Treasury Department authority to intervene if deposit flight started to hurt community banks, according to media reports.

The Federal Reserve's rate decision, to be announced on Wednesday, may also have investors wary of risk assets, including crypto. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee is widely expected to increase its policy rate by 25 basis points, its first hike since 2023.

Crypto stocks slumping the most in Tuesday trading include Circle Internet (CRCL) -11%, Coinbase Global (COIN) -9.2%, Gemini Space Station (GEMI) -8.6%, and Bakkt (BKKT) -7.1%. Crypto mining stocks also dipped: Riot Platforms (RIOT) -5.9%, CleanSpark (CLSK) -5.6%, Core Scientific (CORZ) -4.8%, Hut 8 (HUT) -4.4%, and IREN (IREN) -4.4%.

data.title: 20-year Treasury auction hits record yield as foreign demand plunges
data.description:
The 20-year U.S. Treasury bond (US20Y) (TLT) auction Tuesday revealed market hesitation as foreign demand plummeted.

The $13B auction's 5.420% high yield marks the highest level for the 20-year tenor since its May 2020 reintroduction, up from August’s 5.204%, as long-dated yields keep hitting multi-year highs.

Underscoring the notably soft demand, the final yield tailed the when-issued level of 5.400% by a wide 2.0 basis points—the largest such tail seen since 2024, according to Zerohedge. Furthermore, while the bid-to-cover ratio edged up slightly to 2.57 from last month’s 2.53, it remained sluggish compared with the recent historical average of 2.65.

What's more, indirect bidders, typically a proxy for international investors and foreign central banks, took down a meager 52.5% of the offering. This represents a steep plunge from the previous 62.9% and falls short of the 68.0% recent average, Zerohedge pointed out.

To compensate for the fleeing international capital, domestic participants had to step up. Direct bidders absorbed a record-shattering 30.7% of the auction, surging from 24.6% previously. Consequently, primary dealers were left holding a hefty 16.9% of the supply. Ultimately, the near-record dealer burden emphasizes the growing challenge of finding willing buyers for long-duration government debt without offering significant yield premiums.

The dismal auction arrives against a punishing backdrop for government debt, extending a broader trend of elevated long-term Treasury yields as markets endure a persistent global bond selloff in the face of growing concerns about surging energy prices, rising debt and inflation. Ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision Wednesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield (US10Y) (IEF) climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades, testing the 5% mark.

data.title: Enbridge upgraded at BMO on recent pullback, improving growth visibility
data.description:
Enbridge (ENB) gains 0.6% in Tuesday's trading as BMO Capital upgraded the pipeline operator to Outperform from Market Perform with a C$79.50 price target, saying the stock's recent pullback and improving visibility on growth make an attractive investment in a choppy macroeconomic environment.

Enbridge (ENB) shares have underperformed Canadian midstream and pipeline peers YTD, likely due to rising bond yields, lack of visibility on the company's ~5% growth guidance through the end of the decade, and a recent equity offering, while peers sport higher perceived growth rates, BMO's Ben Pham said.

The analyst said Enbridge (ENB) operates more like a diversified utility, prioritizing premium long-duration contracted assets over higher beta abnormal growth, and believes the company's scale, limited commodity exposure, and diversified assets are underappreciated.

"Few companies can boast a visible premium organic growth program like Enbridge, with its $41B in the secured backlog and $20B of new projects expected to be sanctioned in 2026-27," Pham wrote, while opportunistic acquisitions such as Salt Creek Midstream and the Tallgrass crude transport business come with embedded future upside.

Enbridge's (ENB) ~$3B equity offering and innovative $2.7B joint venture with KKR on its Westcoast B.C. pipeline have shored up the balance sheet, providing additional financial flexibility to fund new growth opportunities that could arise, the analyst said.

data.title: AI chip rally breaks the software–semi link
data.description:
Software delivered its strongest single-day showing versus semiconductors in roughly 25 years on Monday. 

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) advanced +5%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) declined about -5.7%, a spread that reversed the pattern that has defined much of the artificial intelligence cycle.

That cycle had already strained a historically tight link between the two groups. Chipmakers powered the AI build-out and left software far behind, driving their two-year correlation to an unusually weak level. Hardware captured the first wave of capital; application software lagged as investors treated it as a delayed beneficiary—or even a disruption risk. 

Growing debate over whether AI infrastructure spending can keep its recent pace now puts that gap in a different light. A rotation from semiconductors toward lagging software would not require a new bull market in IGV. Even a partial unwind of the extreme relative move could produce meaningful outperformance.
